title: Hamas has agreed to disarm. Israel should now agree to peace – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: Hamas agreed in late July 2026 to a Board of Peace roadmap decommissioning its weapons under a Northern Ireland-style process, but the Board has since rewritten the sequencing so that Israeli withdrawal beyond the Yellow Line begins only after decommissioning is complete — effectively handing Netanyahu an indefinite veto. Lovatt argues Israel, not Hamas, is now the ceasefire's main spoiler, and that Europe's leverage runs through technical support to the new Palestinian police, public documentation of Israeli non-compliance, and reviving the EU-Israel Association Agreement suspension.

insights.claim: At the end of July 2026 Hamas agreed to a Board of Peace roadmap for Phase 2 of the Gaza ceasefire whose core is its willingness to decommission its weapons — a concession the author calls unthinkable a few years ago.
insights.speaker: Hugh Lovatt
insights.so_what: The binding constraint on the Gaza ceasefire has flipped from Palestinian refusal to Israeli refusal — reframe regional risk accordingly.
insights.quote: This would have been unthinkable only a few years ago and offers a realistic pathway for ending the Islamist group’s governance and security control over the devastated Strip.
insights.locator: At the end of July, Hamas agreed

insights.claim: Palestinian heavy weapons are to be handed to the Palestinian National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, locked away under International Stabilisation Force monitoring, and potentially melted down — an explicit replication of Northern Ireland's paramilitary decommissioning model.
insights.speaker: Hugh Lovatt
insights.so_what: The Northern Ireland template implies decommissioning only sticks alongside a parallel political track — judge progress by whether Phase 3 talks start, not by weapons counts.
insights.quote: This would replicate how Northern Ireland’s decommissioning process dealt with weapons held by paramilitary groups.
insights.locator: Heavy weapons will effectively be placed under lock and key

insights.claim: The disarmament scope covers the full range of Palestinian armed groups — many more hardline than Hamas — as well as Israeli-backed militias, with small arms like AK-47s regulated by NCAG through a permit system rather than confiscated.
insights.speaker: Hugh Lovatt
insights.so_what: Partial disarmament is designed into the deal, which is precisely the gap Israel can exploit to claim non-compliance.
insights.quote: This will include the full alphabet soup of Palestinian armed groups—many of which are more hardline than Hamas—as well as Israeli-backed militias.

insights.claim: The implementation machinery is badly under-resourced: NCAG lacks funding, the ISF has only around 200 pledged troops from Morocco with smaller possible contributions from Kosovo and Uganda, and the new Palestinian police force has not begun training in Egypt.
insights.speaker: Hugh Lovatt
insights.so_what: A 200-troop stabilisation force cannot police a 2m-person territory — the deal's operational failure mode is resourcing, not just politics.
insights.quote: the status of the ISF, which to date has only around 200 pledged troops from Morocco, though smaller numbers may also come from countries including Kosovo and Uganda
insights.locator: Questions also remain over the lack of funding

themes.theme: Israel's unfinished Phase 1 and de facto annexation

insights.claim: Israel has not completed its Phase 1 obligations: it has continued striking Gaza, impeded humanitarian aid entry, and advanced its military beyond the Yellow Line it was supposed to withdraw to.
insights.speaker: Hugh Lovatt
insights.so_what: Phase 2 legally cannot begin until Phase 1 closes, so the entire roadmap is stalled at a step Israel controls unilaterally.
insights.quote: The Israeli military has also advanced beyond the Yellow Line, to which it was supposed to withdraw in the first phase.
insights.locator: However, in violation of the agreement

insights.claim: Israel continues demolishing Palestinian homes and infrastructure in the 70% of Gaza still under its control and may be creating a new de facto border to annex a large chunk of the territory, potentially preparing for future Israeli settlements there.
insights.speaker: Hugh Lovatt
insights.so_what: If annexation rather than withdrawal is the operating plan, the ceasefire is a cover for territorial consolidation and will not converge on Phase 3.
insights.quote: Israel has continued to demolish Palestinian homes and infrastructure in the 70% of Gaza that remains under its control

themes.theme: The Board of Peace's sequencing reversal

insights.claim: Board of Peace officials have altered the negotiated deal and their own press release to state that Israeli withdrawal beyond the Yellow Line begins only once decommissioning is complete, contradicting high representative Nikolay Mladenov's initial position that the two would move 'in lockstep'.
insights.speaker: Hugh Lovatt
insights.so_what: The mediator itself has moved toward the Israeli position — the deal's guarantor is no longer a neutral enforcement mechanism.
insights.quote: This appears to contradict the original text and Nikolay Mladenov, the BoP’s high representative, who initially said the two would move forward “in lockstep”.
insights.locator: BoP officials now appear to be altering parts

insights.claim: Conditioning all further Israeli withdrawals on Gaza's full demilitarisation gives Israel a veto over the process, because weapons held by families, clans, criminal networks and jihadi groups make complete removal near-impossible and can be cited indefinitely.
insights.speaker: Hugh Lovatt
insights.so_what: The structural flaw is an unfalsifiable condition — treat announced Israeli withdrawal timelines as non-binding until the sequencing is restored.
insights.quote: the BoP is in effect giving Israel a veto over the process itself, allowing it to deepen its control over the eastern half of Gaza
insights.locator: Moreover, by conditioning all further Israeli withdrawals

insights.claim: Even after the Board of Peace rewrote terms to accommodate Israel, Netanyahu still demands renegotiation and refuses any redeployment — even back to the original Yellow Line — until Hamas fully disarms.
insights.speaker: Hugh Lovatt
insights.so_what: Concessions to Netanyahu have not bought compliance, which argues that pressure rather than accommodation is the only functioning lever.
insights.quote: He continues to demand that the deal be re-negotiated, insisting that no Israeli redeployment will take place, even to the original Yellow Line, until Hamas has fully disarmed.
insights.locator: But even BoP efforts to placate Israel

themes.theme: Leverage: Trump, Europe and Israeli domestic politics

insights.claim: Netanyahu's heavy political investment in portraying his closeness to Trump as an asset is itself the pressure point, since he cannot easily afford a public rupture with a president whose officials have warned he would be 'very, very disappointed' if the deal were derailed.
insights.speaker: Hugh Lovatt
insights.so_what: The highest-signal indicator for the ceasefire holding is US presidential attention, not negotiating-table detail.
insights.quote: Netanyahu has invested heavily in portraying his close relationship with Trump as a political asset—which means he cannot easily afford a public rupture with him

insights.claim: Europe should avoid directly funding the Board of Peace but supply disarmament and security-sector-reform personnel and expertise through the EUPOL COPPS model to support decommissioning and train the new Palestinian police force.
insights.speaker: Hugh Lovatt
insights.so_what: This is the concrete, low-cost channel by which Europe buys back influence after being sidelined — watch for an EUPOL-style mission mandate.
insights.quote: Europe is right to avoid directly funding the BoP.
insights.locator: Europe is right to avoid directly funding

insights.claim: The EU should resume discussions on suspending its Association Agreement with Israel unless Israel complies, and should publicly highlight Israeli non-compliance as Arab and Turkish mediators have done.
insights.speaker: Hugh Lovatt
insights.so_what: A live suspension debate is a tangible trade and market-access risk for Israel's largest trading partner relationship.
insights.locator: Europe can further strengthen his hand

insights.claim: Israel's October elections are a fixed deadline for shifting the domestic debate, but the opposition offers little relief — it attacks Netanyahu for weakness in letting Hamas survive and is unlikely to chart a radical new course on Gaza if it wins.
insights.speaker: Hugh Lovatt
insights.so_what: Do not trade an Israeli election as a Gaza-policy inflection; the distribution of outcomes on the ceasefire is narrow either way.
insights.quote: The Israeli opposition has also been critical of the deal, accusing Netanyahu of weakness by allowing Hamas to survive, and is unlikely to chart a radical new course on Gaza if it wins.
insights.locator: Sustained diplomatic engagement before Israel’s October elections

insights.claim: Without a credible pathway to Palestinian self-determination, decommissioning becomes an end in itself rather than the foundation of a lasting peace, making Phase 3 as important as Phase 2.
insights.speaker: Hugh Lovatt
insights.so_what: Hamas will not finish disarming absent political payoff, so a Phase 2 that is not tied to Phase 3 predictably breaks down.
insights.quote: Without a credible pathway towards Palestinian self-determination, decommissioning risks becoming an end in itself rather than the foundation of a lasting Israeli-Palestinian peace.

insights.claim: The deal only becomes sellable in Israel if it is bundled into a US-brokered regional package, letting a future Israeli government present Gaza withdrawal and a two-state process as the stepping stone to normalisation with Saudi Arabia rather than a unilateral concession.
insights.speaker: Hugh Lovatt
insights.so_what: Saudi normalisation is the currency that pays for Israeli withdrawal — track the regional package, not the Gaza file in isolation.
insights.quote: the indispensable stepping stone towards normalisation with Saudi Arabia and deeper integration with the Arab and Islamic world
